description: The Chefs, founded by three students from Blue Valley West High School. We have participated in hackathons before, and have made top three in all of them. We are skilled in programming (Specifically Java and Python), data calculations, critical thinking, and work very well under a time cramp. We would be welcome to students with the same skills and also as I mentioned, only high school students who are a junior at least.
summary: We, the Chefs, participated in the Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hotspots in the Kansas City Local NASA SpaceApps challenge. We created a website using Python, Shapely, NumPy, pandas, git, Streamlit, and GitHub to make this possible and polished. In the website, there is a visual map, calendar, table, and other graphs/charts to help experts visualize data as best.
details: As said earlier, the website enables experts to better track fire hotspots in the Californian region. We took the MODIS data (which had a larger range) and VIIRS data (which was established post-2002) and synchronized them using a Fire Radiative Power threshold filter. This was to remove any VIIRS background anomalies that MODIS couldn't detect. The visualization of the data provides experts with a map to look at hotspots, a bar chart to show annual/seasonal trends, a burning activity calendar, a peak chart that shows seasonal climatology, a line graph to show the impact of our harmonization, and finally a weekly fire z-score activity tracker. We created this website using Python, Shapely, NumPy, pandas, git, Streamlit, and GitHub to make this possible and polished. Our project is creative because we specifically look at the California region. Also, we incorporated user-friendly devices/tools such as date selectors, sliders, and other sources of input. Some factors we considered were the time gap between MODIS and VIIRS and the area covered by each satellite. This was our submission for the NASA SpaceApps Challenge: Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hotspots. Thank you.
